verdict.tagline: Epic nemesis battles shine despite heavy storage demands and mechanical quirks.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep tactical combat encounters
you like mastering complex skill trees
not_for_you_if: you are short on storage space
you need stable performance on new hardware

cohorts.label: 2-20h

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a very large file size requiring over 150GB of storage space.

citations.review_text: Guess is was just not for me, but after 4 hours in and two years on my SSD I just have to admit I have no intention to ever come back to it and it just takes up precious space (150GB!).

Game has absolutely no business being 151gb download but I promise you it's great, but play shadow of mordor first, please
Play this first and you'll get a little lost in the story and get spoiled because it expands on the systems that were in the previous game
Combat is very nice, akin to the batman arkham series but yknow, swords and magic and cool ♥♥♥♥
This nemesis and recruiting stuff is amazing and I am so unbelievably mad it's patented and won't get used ever again
You can strategize on fortress raids, see what you're up against and choose the units that best suit it, along with what "leaders" you'll be fighting to build your own gear around fighting them too
This game makes you prepare a lot because trust me if you for whatever reason don't have the ability to exploit a weakness, you are going to struggle, especially with enemies that are for example immune to vault-overs, ranged attacks, etc, but it's a fun challenge either way

claims.claim: Reviewers report that enemy captains have unskippable introductory cutscenes that last too long.

citations.review_text: Old game that they only removed the microtransactions from. Yea its fun for a bit. But thats it. The stories arent engaging enough to care. Wish there was skip all story button. Same with the Orc intros. Kinda tired of modding games just to make them fun. Like I said its fun for a little bit, but even with upgrades and skills. Its just the same button mashing, and button countering. That is it. If you want to see the same animations for longs hours of gameplay. If you want to press the same attack button over and over. If you want to hear the same lines from the enemies, ( even if they are suppose to be different orcs)! Then this is for you. TBH the only real fresh feel of the game is SOME of the DLC. But after you unlock the items that is boring too. Even at higher difficulties. There is no change. Same crap over and over.

Great game played it off and on shadow of mordor included and it was almost always peak.

jus hate how theres no option ive found to turn off captain intros, sometimes theyre cool and others it jus lasts tooooooo long

claims.claim: Reviewers state that combat requires learning controls and mastering the kit rather than simply button mashing.

citations.review_text:
Top tier 8.5/10

The Orc bosses Have Personality: The creative work put into the enemy is top-notch. You will develop personal rivalries with guys named "Dirtbag the Ugly" who remembers that time you stabbed them in the head and launched them into a camp fire three days ago, and they've levelled up since then. 

Movement & Combat: The movement is buttery smooth and immensely stylish. Once you get into the rhythm, weaving fluid movement with brutal executes feels phenomenal.

The atmosphere is vivid, and dripping with Lord of the Rings lore. Lore nerds will appreciate the subtle nods scattered throughout. Perfect for booting up when you have an hour to kill and an itch to slay some Uruks.

Skill Curve: The combat takes some getting used to. If you just mash buttons, you’ll develop bad habits and miss out on the best abilities. You genuinely need to slow down, practice the controls, and learn the kit to make the most of it.

Customization: The equipment progression works, but it can get tedious. Gathering loot to upgrade your gear is pretty much the only downside here—customization is a limited.

My only non-complaint? It’s so good that you end up wishing it was a sandbox or RPG and twice as big.

The Verdict: It’s a total gem if you haven't picked it up yet. Absolutely worth your time and coin.

Why are we stealth-killing Orcs anyway? Simply summon a giant eagle........! What do you mean 'Fast Travel is currently unavailable'?!

If you are a fan of LOTR at all, grab this game immediately, especially if it is on sale.

While the story is a little disjointed so far (I did not play the 1st game in this series so that might be the problem), it is still thrilling to be so immersed in the Lord of the Rings world, especially via such an interesting new narrative.

I could easily see myself playing this game for another 200 hours. The combat has a learning curve, but once you get into the flow of things and unlock some additional skills, it becomes quite exciting and addictive.

I just rode my first beast and recently unlocked the second realm. Can't wait to find the time to play some more!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the traversal mechanics feel janky and climbing can be imprecise.

citations.review_text: You are not locked in Minas Ithil with orcs, orcs are locked in Minas Ithil with you. Eh, one of those games with very good ideas that don't quite come together into a very good game. Carving through endless orcs is fun, until it isn't and charm wears thin over slog and jank. YMMV.

This is a fun game. Like the first the traversal can be Janky. But unlike the first this game was infected by the Woke Mind Virus that has since destroyed so many Western Game Studios. Idril is a girl boss with no curves. Baranor is Black and he sticks out like a sore thumb, total DEI casting. But aside from that the game is fun to play.

After completing the game. The worst part of it is every time you come in contact with a captain, War Chief or any other enemy of rank. they always give a speech, and it's always way too long and annoying! They should have at least made them skip able!! But aside from the few mentioned negatives, the game is good and worth playing! The Jankyness is rage inducing at times though!

citations.review_text: Generally a really fun game till you get past level 50. Then any Orc one or two levels above you are incredibly tough and mostly annoying. Not great spending 20 minutes defending an assault just to be taken out by a Captain with the "No Chance" skill. Iron Will is also anti-fun.
Great game if you are a LOTR fan and like fast paced combat. On higher difficulties enemies one shot you, so can be frustrating.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the control scheme as clunky and frustrating because multiple distinct actions are mapped to the same few buttons.

citations.review_text: Really mixed feelings on this one, but overall, I recommend it because I think it's got more strengths and weaknesses, and the nemesis system is something everyone needs to experience once (and probably never again because it's patented but this IP is dead). I think the game's concept is incredible and its potential is sky high, but the experience is held back by clunky controls and a frankly frustrating amount of orcs to battle and manage all at once at every moment. I think just a bit more polish could have made this one of my favorite games ever (so long as you ignore the fan fiction story and murder of the lore), but hey, I still had fun (even though Blade of Galadriel is one of the worst DLCs I've ever played).

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes microtransactions for purchasing captains.

citations.review_text: The Nemesis system is potentially gaming's greatest achievement and that fact that Warner Bros., in all their capitalistic greed, not only decided to sit on it but also added microtransactions into a single-player game that cost 70€ at launch and intentionally made it more grindy to encourage players to spend more money is an indictment of how far their company has fallen after helping publish the Arkham series, the Mad Max game and this game's predecessor. I should've been able to fully celebrate the achievement that was this game but instead it left a sour taste in my mouth that even the incredibly talented folks at Monolith couldn't wash out.

English Version (french below) : 

Hot take but I really do not like this game. It really lost what made the first game so special. 
I mean, you go from forging your weapons' legends and upgrading them by graving elven ruins to now dropping those same weapons because they don't have enough stats and get weird colorful png on the map to get stronger. 

Same thing with the story that completely throws what we know of the lore out of the windows (it was kind of the case with the first one, but this is even more the case here). 
In terms of gameplay, it's still good but it can be very buggy and tedious with just how many perks captains can have against you (it can really get ridiculous at times). 
And let's be real for a minute, buying packs for captains ? Microtransactions in a Lord of the Rings game really leaves a bad taste in my mouth. 

Now, the game is still good in terms of gameplay thanks to the first game, but it became a lot more "video gamey" and lost of lot of what made it "lord of the rings"
The music is okay, but the story and characters are.. kind of weird
It has kind of out of place comic characters that really felt off to me.

The platinum was a bit tedious especially with the DLC and even more with the weird multiplayer castle things with all hackers and just how few people are still on this game.

It's not a "bad" game but I really did not like it for what it stands for.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players encounter high-level immunities and technical snags, yet praise the overall progression and depth.

claims.claim: Side quests can glitch out and fail to work properly, preventing players from continuing the storyline and obtaining certain skill tree sub-skills.

citations.review_text:
I went straight into this game wanting to milk everything I could from this game right after beating and completing every single achievement in the first game (Shadow of Mordor) the goal was to get every achievement from this game as well but after putting many hours in I had hit a road block. There are 2 side quest's that will glitch out and not work properly preventing you from continuing forward with their story line and also not allowing you to obtain a few sub skills in the skill tree. Apparently this glitch has been known for years and hasn't been fixed at all which is super frustrating especially with such a huge title. After doing research through forums to see if there were any solutions or fixes that I could try there were next to none that worked for me so I gave up. I would not recommend this game if you plan on 100% the game.
But if you're a casual and don't care for achievements then I would highly recommend the game due to the massive improvements in gameplay and world building of the story.
Gameplay 9/10
Story 7.5/10

A very flawed gem.

The Nemesis System that the gameplay loop is dependent on has so much potential, but is bogged down by (1.) lots of bugs that make long-term play unsustainable and (2.) Warner Bros. decision to copyright the system and then refuse to develop it any further (they're sitting on for no reason other than to stop other companies from implementing something similar, lest WB sue them if the new system resembles the Nemesis System in ANY way).

Furthermore, Online Conquest is absolutely unplayable in 2026 due to rampant modded enemy Orcs that are essentially unkillable and bugs that replace your own dominated orcs with random enemies over time. It's truly infuriating to think that this game once had microtransactions that allowed you to purchase Orc Captains for real money, only for them to be potentially replaced by randomly spawned enemies.

As with almost all my other reviews, the synopsis of this one is that litigious corporations that make games are the problem. I continue to feel sorry for developers who have them as parent companies and are working hard to develop groundbreaking ew technologies and systems under the thumb of greedy corporations like Warner Bros.

What can I say about Middle-earth: Shadow of War? Possibly one of the most interesting and replayable games of all time. My uncle got me into it back in 2017, I remember watching him play it on an old pc he and my dad had built, and being amazed by all the different and cool looking orcs he was fighting (the shiny marauder orcs were my personal favorite!). When I finally started playing the game myself, I immediately fell in love with the character of Talion and the story in general. So, yes there are microtransactions, yes online is busted with hacked orcs beyond measure, but none of that matters to me because this is THE GAME for me. Oh and dont even get me started on Baranor's DLC, super fun and even Eltariel's DLC grew on me after a while... ♥♥♥♥ I might just be a glazer atp

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes side quests and missions that act as training tutorials for new weapons and skills.

citations.review_text:
I bought this game in 2017 when it came out but never really played it. Now, after 10 years, I have decided to take another look at it. It’s July 2026, and I have two missions left before the game is won; it has been an enjoyable experience.
Pros: Nemesis system: Regenerates Captains you have beaten / Levels up Captains that have killed you; providing never-ending, challenging gameplay. Large skill tree to keep combat fresh, varied and accommodating to a variety of combat styles. Combat is smooth, very good -reminds me of the Batman Arkham series games. Graphics hold up well for a game that is 10 years old. Automatic game saves are frequent enough that you don’t have to repeat large segments of the game if you die. Action is non-stop, never ending. Cons: I don’t know if there is much of a story here and that is only a negative if you are looking for a story driven game. This game does not follow Middle Earth canon, so calibrate your expectations. There are a few easy puzzles to solve, some side missions / quests that serve as training tutorials for new weapons / skills. Some may feel that is somewhat of a grind to get through all of these, but it does help diversify your playstyle.

Decent story, but it does rely pretty heavily on players being interested in the Lord Of The Rings universe and lore. The gameplay is a lot of fun though, the Nemesis System helps keep you on your toes and forces players to not rely on a single strategy for defeating captains as they will often adapt and become immune to fighting styles that are used repeatedly on them.

My only real complaint is the frequency of enemy ambushes. Whenever I go to take out one captain, I'm almost guaranteed to be ambushed by at least one other captain, and usually when I'm already fighting a horde of grunts and the first captain. I just did a mission where I was literally ambushed during the ambush that happened during the ambush of my mission, which was also an ambush mission. This is the type of ambush-ception crap that would get Christopher Nolan rock-hard. 5 enemy captains, about 20 grunts, and the only saving grace was that 2 of the captains were also fighting each other as part of the original mission I had started. Keeping my distance from those 2 let them focus on each other while I handled all of the ambushers.

Insanely fun gameplay though, and the game as a whole is really polished and continues to run great and look great on modern hardware. Definitely worth the purchase price these days, especially if it's on sale.

I'm giving this a thumbs down simply because the game does a fantastic job of ruining itself, something especially abhorrent in a game with such an excellent premise.

In an effort to keep the game challenging you end up fighting enemies that are immune to your entire skillset, making all of your hard earned levels and talent tree choices completely irrelevant. The only thing left to you "combat-wise" is to run away and shoot arrows from afar or (because they are immune to that too) keep recruiting allies until they eventually do the job for you.
This strategy won't always work either, resulting on a very strong feeling of "it really doesn't matter what I do here, I'm going to lose".

The game is about being a bad-ass one man army slaying machine and I so wish it just allowed itself to be that.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that enemy captains interrupt gameplay with unskippable dialogue and speeches during active combat.

citations.review_text: Except alot interrupts gameplay in middle battle with boss speaking, all others aspects is nice.

This game is almost the same as Shadow of Mordor. However, the first thing you'll notice after loading in is how the camera controls became worse – feeling slippery to the point the camera keeps moving even after the mouse stops. This can be somewhat mitigated by turning down the mouse sensitivity down to the minimum setting, which will make it more comparable to the medium of Shadow of Mordor. If you can get past the slight left-over acceleration.

What you won't be able to get past is that now the orks became even more chatty. Previously, they would stop you mid-charge to tell you how you're about to die. Now, they will stop you mid-charge to tell you their entire life's story. And also how you're about to die. These interruptions in the flow of action cannot be turned off or skipped, making them even more jarring than before. And of course half the time the camera is in the middle of returning to third-person view (and you don't have control of your character yet) you can get hit and even killed by random attacks you had no way of dodging.

Contrary to the reforging system of the previous game, here you can (and have to) swap out your gear for new ones you get from killing orcs. The weapons that were reforged in the first game, have also been returned to their basic, unupgraded form. You might think that this was done to preserve Talion's identity, but the weapons get reforged again by the end of the story. The story that is still as abrupt as it was in the previous game, but now Talion is even more of a pushover.

An other thing that was made worse is the map. In Shadow of Mordor, the map was a very useful blueprint that showed you exactly where what was. Now the map is more of a loose diorama, that only approximately ties into the actual game you're playing. But, you can rotate it! If you were crazy enough to actually bother and throw away any semblance of where North is. The mouse sensitivity on the map is also too high and can't be reduced. The last par…
